effects: The signer sends exactly `assets` WBTC to the vault, using the signer's WBTC allowance to the vault (ERC4626._deposit safeTransferFrom).
The vault mints gtWBTCc shares to `receiver`. The number is computed from the vault's exchange rate after fee accrual (MetaMorpho.deposit, _convertToSharesWithTotals, rounded down).
formats.shown: Intent 'Deposit', the exact WBTC amount, the share ticker gtWBTCc as a constant, and the receiver of the shares.

findings.title: deposit: the intent is just 'Deposit', with no amount, asset or vault, and there is no interpolatedIntent
findings.evidence: descriptor.json deposit format: "intent": "Deposit" with no interpolatedIntent; the amount appears only in the 'Deposit asset' field.
findings.fix: Add an interpolatedIntent such as 'Deposit {assets} into Gauntlet gtWBTCc vault for {receiver}'.

findings.title: deposit: the number of shares received is not shown because the contract computes it from storage
findings.evidence: MetaMorpho.sol deposit: shares = _convertToSharesWithTotals(assets, totalSupply(), newTotalAssets, Floor). Case 0: signer received 9887330253267 gtWBTCc, and the screen shows only the 'Share ticker' gtWBTCc.
findings.fix: No calldata holds this value. A label such as 'Receive gtWBTCc shares (at vault rate)' could set expectations.

cases.notes: The 0.00001 WBTC outflow is shown correctly. The share inflow is shown with its asset and receiver but no amount, which is a spec limitation.

effects: The signer pays WBTC to the vault, using the signer's WBTC allowance. The amount is computed from `shares` at the vault exchange rate, rounded up (MetaMorpho.mint, _convertToAssetsWithTotals Ceil), and there is no maximum in calldata.
The vault mints exactly `shares` gtWBTCc to `receiver`.
formats.shown: Intent 'Mint', 'Deposit asset: WBTC' with no amount, the exact shares minted in gtWBTCc, and the receiver of the shares.

findings.title: mint: the WBTC amount taken from the signer is not shown, and no bound exists in calldata
findings.evidence: MetaMorpho.sol mint: assets = _convertToAssetsWithTotals(shares, totalSupply(), newTotalAssets, Math.Rounding.Ceil); then _deposit pulls `assets` from the caller. Case 1: 101 WBTC left the signer, but the screen shows only 'Deposit asset: WBTC'.
findings.fix: No calldata holds this value. Relabel to something like 'Pay with (amount set by vault rate)' so the signer knows the WBTC cost is not fixed.

findings.title: mint: the intent 'Mint' does not say that WBTC is paid or who receives the shares
findings.evidence: descriptor.json mint format: "intent": "Mint" with no interpolatedIntent. The case 1 reader could not tell how much WBTC leaves.
findings.fix: Add an interpolatedIntent such as 'Mint {shares} by depositing WBTC, shares to {receiver}'.

cases.notes: The signer paid 101 WBTC, and the screen shows the asset but no amount. The shares went to 0xdead (signer null), shown correctly as the receiver.

formats.key: withdraw(uint256 assets, address receiver, address owner)
effects: The vault burns gtWBTCc shares from `owner`. The number is computed and rounded up (MetaMorpho.withdraw, _convertToSharesWithTotals Ceil).
When the signer is not `owner`, the call spends the signer's share allowance from `owner` (ERC4626._withdraw _spendAllowance).
The vault sends exactly `assets` WBTC to `receiver`.
formats.shown: Intent 'Withdraw', the exact WBTC amount, the receiver, and the owner whose shares are used.

findings.title: withdraw: the number of shares burned from the owner is not shown because it is computed from storage
findings.evidence: MetaMorpho.sol withdraw: shares = _convertToSharesWithTotals(assets, totalSupply(), newTotalAssets, Math.Rounding.Ceil); _withdraw burns them from owner.
findings.fix: No calldata holds this value. A label noting that gtWBTCc shares are burned would help.

findings.title: withdraw: the intent is just 'Withdraw', with no amount, asset or recipient
findings.evidence: descriptor.json withdraw format: "intent": "Withdraw" with no interpolatedIntent.
findings.fix: Add an interpolatedIntent such as 'Withdraw {assets} from gtWBTCc vault to {receiver}'.

formats.key: redeem(uint256 shares, address receiver, address owner)
effects: The vault burns exactly `shares` gtWBTCc from `owner`. When the signer is not the owner, the call spends the signer's share allowance from `owner`.
The vault sends WBTC to `receiver`. The amount is computed from shares at the vault rate, rounded down (MetaMorpho.redeem, _convertToAssetsWithTotals Floor), and there is no minimum in calldata.
formats.shown: Intent 'Redeem', the exact gtWBTCc shares, the receiver and the owner. Nothing says that WBTC is received.

findings.title: redeem: the asset received (WBTC) is never named on the screen
findings.evidence: descriptor.json redeem format has the fields shares, receiver and owner only. mint uses the constant $.metadata.constants.underlyingTicker, and redeem has no such field. Case 2: the signer received 540167 WBTC, and the reader only guessed 'likely WBTC'.
findings.fix: Add a constant field {"label":"Receive asset","format":"raw","value":"$.metadata.constants.underlyingTicker"} and an interpolatedIntent such as 'Redeem {shares} for WBTC to {receiver}'.

findings.title: redeem: the WBTC amount received is not shown and has no minimum, because the vault rate decides it
findings.evidence: MetaMorpho.sol redeem: assets = _convertToAssetsWithTotals(shares, totalSupply(), newTotalAssets, Math.Rounding.Floor). Case 2: 540167 WBTC in, and no amount is on the screen.

findings.title: redeem: the intent is just 'Redeem', with no amount, asset or recipient
findings.evidence: descriptor.json redeem format: "intent": "Redeem" with no interpolatedIntent.
findings.fix: Add an interpolatedIntent naming the shares, the WBTC and the receiver.

cases.notes: The gtWBTCc burn is shown exactly. The WBTC inflow is not named and has no amount; the reader guessed the asset. The ENS name hid whether the receiver is the signer's own address.
